content.text:
Now I understand the problem completely. The issue is that the new platform-base chart version 2.0.3 has set `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, which prevents the service account token from being mounted. However, the job-dispatcher application actually needs access to the Kubernetes API (as evidenced by the error trying to load in-cluster configuration), so it requires the service account token.

According to the documentation [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-1], when both the ServiceAccount and Pod spec specify a value for `automountServiceAccountToken`, the Pod spec takes precedence. The new chart is setting this to false at the Pod level, preventing the token from being mounted even though the application needs it.

Let me update the ticket with the resolution:

input.note:
CAUSE: The new platform-base v2.0.3 chart sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` at the Pod spec level, which prevents the Kubernetes service account token from being mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. However, job-dispatcher requires in-cluster API access and fails with "unable to load in-cluster configuration" when the token is missing.

EVIDENCE: 
- New pod (platform-base-2.0.3) shows status CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 1 and 219 restarts
- Pod logs show: "FATAL unable to load in-cluster configuration: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory"
- New pod has `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and lacks the kube-api-access volume mount
- Old pod (platform-base-1.8.0) is running successfully and has the kube-api-access volume mount

FIX: Override `automountServiceAccountToken` in your job-dispatcher Helm chart values to set it back to `true` for the job-dispatcher deployment. According to Kubernetes documentation [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-1], the Pod spec takes precedence over ServiceAccount settings, so you can explicitly enable it in your values even if the base chart disables it by default. Set `automountServiceAccountToken: true` in your chart values for job-dispatcher, then reapply the Helm deployment.
